synopsis: EDEM is described as commercial discrete-element modeling software for bulk materials such as soil, ore and coal, with coupling to vehicle and multibody simulation [f8587, f15985, f9134]. Its strongest relevance is mining, quarrying and earth interaction; Chapter 8 gives a concrete tracked-machine soft-soil workflow using Altair MotionSolve/MotionView coupled to EDEM [f8588, f6388]. It is not a perception or ADAS simulator, and its sensor capabilities are listed as not applicable, so its role in collision-mitigation validation is machine–terrain physics rather than sensor simulation [f8590, f9136, f16074]. DEM is computationally expensive, while public pricing and the latest release date were not found, leaving cost and release currency unresolved [f8589, f8591]. The glossary explicitly flags that Chapter 11 calls the tool Siemens Simcenter EDEM whereas Chapter 8 cites an Altair workflow, leaving a naming/vendor-attribution tension to clarify [f15986, f8587, f6388].
